parsed.why: Strong local public-accommodation protections, functioning complaint relief, healthcare shield, and no facility ban materially improve local exposure. National passport, entry-screening, and federal-facility risks remain operative.

No documented local facility restriction and some discrimination protections, but little demonstrated visitor-facing protection beyond the adverse national regime; unresolved X-marker practice and limited local evidence keep the improvement modest.

Operating shield protections, gender-identity facility safeguards, identity-congruent custody rules, and broad protections make this the strongest local layer. National document, border, and federally controlled-setting exposures still apply.

Broad operative protections, shield laws, mandated gender-neutral bathrooms, and repeal of police harassment provisions substantially mitigate local exposure. A county sports restriction and the hostile national border and facility regime remain.

The state adds hostile care restrictions, including for people in custody, and stringent local document rules with no general gender-identity nondiscrimination law. These compound the national risks, though no local bathroom ban is documented.
